desk.headline: Record revenue up 13.5% to $1.99bn, in line; AFFO per share beat; 2026 guidance raised and dividend lifted 15%
results: Record Q3 revenue of $1.99bn, up 13.5%: storage rental +11% to $1.15bn and services +17% to $841m.
Data centre revenue jumped 34% to $274m and asset lifecycle management (ALM) 43%; the three growth businesses grew more than 30% combined.
Signed a record 102 MW of data centre leases in the quarter, 137 MW so far this year.
AFFO rose 17% to $458m ($1.53 a share); adjusted EBITDA was a record $748m.
Quarterly dividend raised 15% to $0.993; leverage was 4.8x, inside the 4.5–5.5x target.

guidance.summary: Iron Mountain raised its 2026 outlook again, now seeing revenue of $7.95–8.02bn and AFFO of $5.94–6.00 a share, despite a stronger dollar. For Q4 it expects about $2.03bn of revenue and $1.57 of AFFO per share.

points: Data centre pricing is rising; renewals came in about 10% higher on a cash basis, and the backlog supports about $1.7bn of yearly revenue.
CEO Bill Meaney expects 2027 to be "another 20% plus year" for data centres, with about 325 MW due to come online within 24 months.
ALM is now expected to top $1bn of revenue in 2026, with enterprise ALM growing over 50% organically.
A stronger dollar trims Q4 revenue by roughly $5–10m versus the prior plan, already built into guidance.
More data centre construction means higher borrowing; current debt due within a year rose to $1.23bn.
call.source: Earnings presentation (Exhibit 99.2); call transcript via Earnings Whispers; 24/7 Wall St., 5 Nov 2026

watch: Conversion of the data centre lease backlog into revenue and new leasing in Q4.
Storage rental margins, which fell year on year.
Debt and funding costs as data centre construction speeds up.
